items.title: POV: auction day
items.text:
POV: IPL auction day.
You've got twenty-seven crore and the biggest paddle.
Your analyst waves a spreadsheet.
You wave back.
Sold! Confetti!
Except.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Seven beat an average player.
Everyone else? Nearly four in ten.
The two big hits were both captains.
Turns out most of that price was hype.
Next year, give the analyst the paddle.

items.title: I spent ₹27 crore on one player
items.text:
I spent twenty-seven crore on one cricketer.
My analyst tried to stop me.
I thought he was waving hello.
The room went mad. Then someone checked.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Seven beat an average player.
Seven.
The two that worked? Both wore the armband.
Turns out you mostly pay for the hype.
My analyst's got the paddle now.
He's bidding base price.

items.title: The star or the bargain bin?
items.text:
Would you rather have the IPL auction's most expensive player, or three cheap ones?
Careful.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Only seven beat an average player.
Everyone else bought? Nearly four in ten did.
The two big hits were both captains.
Big prices mostly buy hype.
So. The star, or the bargain bin?
Your analyst already knows.
Tell us in the comments.
